criteria.idempotent_open: Let carrier authentication plus a fresh nonce open the door, then resolve everything from delivery_id: done answers done, dead answers dead, unknown answers 404, unsettled stays pending while banking the attempt row. Ownership of the lease plays no part. Correctness rests on delivery_id dedup downstream and one-way delivery transitions.
criteria.ownership_checked: Accept reports solely from the lease holder by matching worker_id with version, answering 409 lease_lost otherwise. Workers that lost the race or lease must reclaim before their ack lands. Attribution is stricter; the price is extra conflict branches and reclaim flows in the companion.

ack.instructions: Must an ack prove the reporter still owns the lease, or is carrier authentication with idempotent per-delivery handling the better contract?

criteria.multi_batch: Sweep up to K rows per claim transaction through an in-decision recursive loop, leasing each row under version guard. Round trips shrink, but the decision gains recursion, per-depth mocks, and a broader assertion burden for the same per-row guarantees.
criteria.single_page: Take no more than one row per claim: lookup-first read of the oldest claimable row, then a conditional write pinned to its version. Can stays linear and each arm mocks directly; the companion loops to empty and re-issues after race misses. Paging and batching remain companion duties.

claim.instructions: Should the claim call gather multiple rows per round trip, or gather one row per call with the companion looping?

criteria.bearer_nonce: Present the shared secret as a bearer header together with a fresh timestamp and one-time nonce. Can stays trivial and no signature is computed per call. Replay inside the window still fails on the nonce record, but modified payloads pass silently, leaving integrity to loopback/trusted scope and the deployment transport.
criteria.body_fields: Carry timestamp_ms plus nonce within the signed JSON payload itself; headers bear just the protocol version and the HMAC-SHA-256 hex of the precise bytes. This replays the proven provider-side pattern, skips canonical assembly, ties all fields into one tag, and turns replays into nonce collisions.
criteria.header_canonical: Carry timestamp, nonce and tag in headers and sign a canonical join of timestamp, nonce, method, path and body. Both route and content sit under the tag, while Can absorbs canonical building and header extraction. Nonce records continue to defeat replay.

envelope.instructions: Which carrier-call authentication envelope should the versioned protocol adopt?

state.constraints: The Can toolkit at hand: exact-byte HMAC-SHA-256 already demonstrated on provider intake, size-capped JSON payloads, integer arithmetic alongside ordering tests, text::join for canonical assembly, JSON integer timestamps checked against the wall clock, transactions pairing conditional UPDATE with affected-row feedback, and a single-use nonce table. Only SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE descriptors without RETURNING are admitted. Decisions touching one row read linearly; decisions touching many need recursion and depth-indexed mocks. Comparison stays exact yet not constant-time, documented as a limit.
state.criteria: Adopt the most compact approach that fixes R16-03, preserves at-least-once delivery with idempotent ack while two workers contend, rides out supervisor restarts on idempotency alone, mocks and asserts tidily, and exposes honest versioned failures through C-E statuses.
state.decided: P09-B3 already locks the contours: portable lookup-first claim_outbox(worker_id, lease_until) over lease-table rows, with locking reads explicitly out; worker identity, lease expiry and heartbeat versioned into the protocol; at-least-once delivery paired with idempotent ack under C-C unknown-write language; beyond N versioned tries the companion reports the row through dead_letter and Can retains the table plus decide_ack dead-letter rules; supervisor-driven companion restarts redeliver unacked work with no further Can-side recovery. F-R11-04 keeps loopback and trusted-carrier framing. There are no outside users, no compatibility shims, and secrets ride environment snapshots only.
state.goal: Ship F05: the authenticated pairing of the Can webhook program with its operating companion. Can retains ledger, outbox, attempt history, idempotent decide/ack transactions and commit-unknown reconciliation; the companion absorbs claiming, downstream delivery, retry schedules, capped concurrency, poison routing, crash recovery and destination policy checks. Closing R16-03 means carrier endpoints authenticate, so unauthenticated, replayed and malformed carrier calls all fail closed.
state.threats: Plan for replayed carrier calls, bodies rewritten between processes, and an extra worker contending for the same leases. Simultaneous claims must resolve to a single winner with no repeated business outcome; doubled downstream posts collapse through delivery_id dedup instead of through any exactly-once pretense. Environment snapshots alone carry secrets, logs never do, and responses keep C-E honesty across 200/400/401/404/409/413/503, always with a body.
